correctness.rationale: For every n=(2^k−1)2^j≥3 and every signed edge set A, exact expansion into forced-edge subsets and the path contraction formula N_n(F)=2^(h−1)(n−t−1)! show that all nonempty terms are 0 modulo 2^(nu2(M_n)+1). The digit-record inequality s2(n−1−t)≤s2(n−1) and Legendre valuation verify this for t≤n−3, and the factor 2^t settles t≥n−2. M_n=(n−1)!/2 has exact two-adic order n−2−s2(n−1), so all Walsh coefficients have that order and are nonzero. Full exact Walsh computations n=3..8, independent signed DP n≤7 and n=12,14,15,16, and the two counterexamples have been actually replayed. Computations corroborate rather than establish the infinite case.

value.rationale: The complete-graph Hamiltonian-cycle orbit is a canonical edge-incidence subset with a natural exact Walsh support and convolution-invertibility question. The theorem supplies a nontrivial exact arithmetic valuation uniform across every sign assignment for infinitely many dimension orders and yields full Fourier support. Zero sums at n=5 and n=9 show the digit condition is a real structural boundary; this is more than a textbook identity or an isolated tiny computation. No unsupported claim is made about optimality or all excluded orders.
